title: The runtime
about: `packages/agent-runtime` runs agent sessions on a harness, durably: its words are what a session is and how it runs.

terms.meaning: the protocol the runtime uses for every harness; each harness is an A2A agent, and a session is an A2A Task.

a queued task's word to start, given by `admit` or by the engine under its ceiling and, while it keeps a `reserved` floor, the machine's memory: the requests of what holds a slot within its total, and the newcomers within what is available now.

why a pass left a queued task waiting, journalled as a `waits` entry when it changes and said on its view while it is queued: its pool at the ceiling (`slot`, with the pool and the ceiling) or the machine's memory (`memory`, with its need and the room there was), as a Pod's PodScheduled condition says Unschedulable. A status: no rule reads it (`packages/agent-runtime/src/core/admission.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/core/engine/engine.ts`).
why the Task door refused an append, on `JournalError.reason`: `malformed-id`, `filed-twice`, `not-filed` or `attempt-out-of-order`.

one start of a task's session, numbered n and named `ae/<task>/<n>`: a restart inside one task, the way a container's restart count goes up inside one Pod, and never a try, which is the layer above's filing of a new task. Whatever ends it settles the task.
an attempt's number within its task: a task's attempts number from 1 with no gap.

a word a harness's declaration lists: a key of a task's config it takes, a kind of session it keeps, or an Engine verb it answers. A task that asks its harness for one it does not declare is refused, naming the harnesses that do.
whether an attempt's session gave the closing statement its task asked for, as its end reported it: a fact the runtime records and the layer above judges.

terms.meaning: what one harness says it can do, once: its capabilities (`can`) and the data its checks read beside them (its knobs, context range, fence reach, the config its neutral asks become). A harness is its declaration plus its driver; a runner a consumer brings as its own declares nothing and is asked nothing.

a word that holds new tool calls at their hook, read off a file on every look: the holder's drain (`drain`), put for the attached sessions of one holding process across its restart, and the sessions' drain (`drainSessions`), store-wide, which every Claude Code job reads on each poll, every holder for its attached sessions, and the engine's pass on each pass (`Now.drained`), which pauses the deadlines only of tasks whose harness declares `drain` (`packages/agent-runtime/src/core/engine/drain.ts`, the runtime's own record). A call in flight finishes within the sessions' drain's grace (`graceMs`: the store's pause timeout, as the orchestrator hands it on) and is cut past it; a parked job is continued, and a cut attached session told, only once the sessions' drain is lifted; a re-put with the same grace keeps its start. Two independent facts: lifting one never lifts the other.

terms.meaning: the runtime's loop: it compares each task's journal with what the harness lists, and asks `decide` what to do.
where a task's session runs: the host, the only place there is, so a task names none.
the program a session runs in: Claude Code, Codex, a plain command, or a remote A2A agent.

terms.meaning: what a task gives its harness — model, tools, mounts and the rest — carried to it, never read by `decide`.

the version of the harness a session's process runs, as the harness says it: Claude Code's init message's `claude_code_version`, the last one it printed. Recorded on the attempt while it works (`harnessVersion`), carried and never judged.

a session's main-thread tool call waiting at its hook while a drain stands, and since when, with the call it stopped after (`after`): carried on its sighting, never judged, so a person sees the session is held and not stalled. The engine journals when an attempt is first seen held and when it is seen released (`held`, `released`), and a deadline counts again from the release.

the code a session's process runs, as that process reports it: the real folder of the runtime package that spawned or holds it, a Pod's container image. Recorded on the attempt while it works (`image`), a long-lived session's rewritten by each new holder; what release it is, is the layer above's to say.
the runtime's durable record of a task, an event a line, which every pass reads again; read and written through the Task door alone.
an event of a task's journal, with the task it belongs to, in any shape a runtime has written; the Task door gives it with its task's `TaskId`.
the statechart a runtime task moves along.
one move of a task through the lifecycle, as its journal says it: the entry's kind and when.

terms.meaning: what Claude Code loads an MCP server of a `.mcp.json` over, in the Agent SDK's words for a server a file declares (`MCP_TRANSPORTS`: stdio, http, sse); a written `type` that is none of them reads as `unknown` (`transportOf`).

a task's `resources.limits.memory`, a Kubernetes quantity (`8Gi`), or, where it names none, its engine's `defaultLimits` in force as each attempt starts, recorded on its `starting` entry: its harness and every child it starts run in a transient scope of systemd's user manager under that `MemoryMax=`, so a process passing it is killed by the kernel in that cgroup alone, and the attempt records what the cgroup saw (`memory`: `limitBytes`, `peakBytes`, `oomKills`). A host that cannot make the scope refuses a limited task `unstartable` (`packages/agent-runtime/src/harness/cgroup.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/core/memory.ts`).

a task's `resources.requests.memory`, a Kubernetes quantity, or, where it names no resources, its engine's `defaultRequests` in force when it is admitted and as each attempt starts, recorded on its `starting` entry: what admission counts it at against the machine's memory, its limit standing for it where it gives none, as Kubernetes gives a container that names a limit and no request. Refused above its limit (`packages/agent-runtime/src/core/admission.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/core/engine/filing.ts`).
a folder beyond a task's `cwd` its session may reach, and whether it may only read it.
how an attempt ended and how a task settled: one word for both, `succeeded`, `failed` or `stopped`. A journal's former `done` is read as `succeeded`.

a job that ended itself under a sessions' drain, past the drain's grace with a call in flight or held past its bound, or that crashed while held or draining, with the call it cut (`calling`) where it cut one. A fact on its end beside its state, never an end reason: once the drain is lifted the runtime continues it as the next attempt of the same task, resumed in its session and told the call that did not finish, with what is left of its spend cap (`parkedCapLeft`, built on `capLeft`).
where a task stands for a reader, from its record plus one observation: a closed literal, never a sentence. The harness's own state of the attempt in flight is beside it, as `session` (A2A's names).

terms.meaning: the engine's `reserved.memory`, the floor kept off the machine for the daemon and the machine itself, as kubelet's system-reserved: given, each pass reads the machine's memory once (`/proc/meminfo`) and admits by it beside the ceiling (`packages/agent-runtime/src/service/options.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/service/machine.ts`).

terms.meaning: `packages/agent-runtime`, which runs agent sessions on a harness, durably.
one agent's conversation on a harness: a job that runs to its end, or a long-lived session that runs until stopped.

see.label: A job and a long-lived session

terms.meaning: a call of a session's held for a person where its task says one can be asked (`mayAsk`), of one of two kinds (`SessionAskKind`): a `question` the session asked through `AskUserQuestion`, or a `permission`, a call Claude Code would prompt for, asked as one question whose choices are allow once, always allow and deny, beside what the SDK said of it (`PermissionFacts`). Written down once as open, answered through the session's answers file or cut by its turn's end, and carried on its sighting (`asks`).
the harness's own id for a session, the one `--resume` takes: the runtime reads it and never checks it.

the transient scope of systemd's user manager a local session's process tree runs in, wherever the host makes one, under its memory limit where it has one: every process its commands start sits in it, wherever started from, and is ended with it — SIGTERM, then `cgroup.kill` past the stop grace — the release refused while anything is left. Its folder is recorded on the session's run file (`cgroup`), and only a scope `scopeToEnd` allows is ended, never the cgroup the runtime runs in. An unlimited session whose scope is refused runs bare and says why (`unscoped`) (`packages/agent-runtime/src/harness/cgroup.ts`, `packages/agent-runtime/src/harness/scope.ts`).
where the runtime keeps its tasks' journals and feed (`AE_ROOT`).

terms.meaning: in A2A, a client following one Task's events as they happen.
the runtime's unit of work: a brief filed to run on a harness, with its attempts.

the one way a task's journal is read and written (`Journal`, any store given through `Journal.layer`): its ids branded, and an append that breaks a task's invariants refused before any store is written.
a task's id, the name of its journal file, branded `TaskId` at the Task door: checked on a new filing, read as any string.

where a harness's transcript event came from, as the harness said it: one of the Agent SDK's words for a message's origin (`ORIGIN_KINDS`: human, channel, peer, task-notification, coordinator, unclassified, observer, auto-continuation, observer-activity), or `unknown` for any word the SDK has not named, never read as a person's (`originOf`).
